AbstractText.Label: BACKGROUND
AbstractText.content: Pregnant women with heart disease (HD) have higher rates of adverse fetal outcomes. We describe placental pathologic characteristics and their association with fetal events.

AbstractText.Label: METHODS
AbstractText.content: In pregnant women, known HD were categorized into: (1) cardiomyopathy (CM) or (2) other HD (congenital, coronary, arrhythmia, or valvular). Outcomes were maternal major adverse cardiac events (MACE), fetal adverse clinical events (FACE), a composite of infant death, prematurity, underweight status, intracranial hemorrhage, and respiratory distress. Only pathologically reported placental analyses were included.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: We studied 86 pregnancies in women with CM and HD, with pathologic analyses on 35 CM and 52 HD placentas. CM placentas, compared with those with HD, were more likely to have ischemic changes (65.7% vs. 37%, p 0.008), demonstrate immaturity (62.90% vs. 10%, p < 0.001), and have a lower weight (p < 0.001), despite similar gestational age. CM was independently associated with increased risk for MACE (OR 7.38, 95%CI 2.20-24.76). Ischemic placental changes were associated with increased odds of FACE (OR 24.78, 95%CI 2.37-259.03).

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSIONS
AbstractText.content: Women with CM were more likely to have ischemic placentas, with lower placental and fetal weights, and evidence of immaturity compared with those with other forms of HD, and an increased odds of MACE.
